must_show.claim: Tyrannosaurus was a bipedal carnivore with a massive skull balanced by a long, heavy tail.
must_show.quote: Like other tyrannosaurids, Tyrannosaurus was a bipedal carnivore with a massive skull balanced by a long, heavy tail.

must_show.claim: The skull was extremely wide at the rear but had a narrow snout, allowing unusually good binocular vision.
must_show.quote: It was extremely wide at the rear but had a narrow snout, allowing unusually good binocular vision.

must_show.claim: The neck was exceptionally short, deep and muscular to support the massive head.
must_show.quote: Compared to these, it was exceptionally short, deep and muscular to support the massive head.

must_show.claim: The hindlimbs were among the longest in proportion to body size of any theropod.
must_show.quote: In contrast to the arms, the hindlimbs were among the longest in proportion to body size of any theropod.

Tyrannosaurus rex.why: Massive skull, narrow snout, short deep neck, long hindlimbs; no crest or sail.

must_show.claim: Its skull was low.
must_show.quote: Though incompletely known, the skull of Giganotosaurus appears to have been low.

must_show.claim: The front of its lower jaw was flattened and had a downward-pointing chin at the tip.
must_show.quote: The front of the lower jaw was flattened and had a downward-projecting process (or "chin") at the tip.

must_show.claim: It had rough, wrinkled nasal bones and a ridge-like crest on the bone in front of the eye.
must_show.quote: The skull was low, with rugose (rough and wrinkled) nasal bones and a ridge-like crest on the lacrimal bone in front of the eye.

Giganotosaurus.why: Low skull, downward chin, ridge-like crest; no sail or horns.

must_show.claim: It had a long, low skull with an upturned snout.
must_show.quote: Velociraptor can be distinguished from other dromaeosaurids by its long and low skull, with an upturned snout.

must_show.claim: It had a large hand with three long fingers ending in strongly curved claws.
must_show.quote: Velociraptor, like other dromaeosaurids, had a large manus with three elongated digits (fingers), which ended up in strongly curved unguals (claw bones) that were similar in construction and flexibility to the wing bones of modern birds.

must_show.claim: It had a sickle-shaped claw on its foot that could grow to over 6.5 cm long.
must_show.quote: This enlarged claw, which could grow to over 6.5 cm (2.6 in) long around its outer edge, was most likely a predatory device used to restrain struggling prey.

must_show.claim: It had a long tail.
must_show.quote: It was a bipedal, feathered carnivore with a long tail and an enlarged sickle-shaped claw on each hindfoot, which is thought to have been used to tackle and restrain prey.

must_show.claim: It had feathers.
must_show.quote: Velociraptor was warm blooded and had feathers.

Velociraptor.why: Upturned snout, long three-fingered hands, sickle claw, long tail; feathers.

must_show.claim: Allosaurus had distinctive horns above its eyes.
must_show.quote: It had three-fingered hands and distinctive horns above its eyes.

must_show.claim: Allosaurus had a broad rib cage giving it a barrel chest.
must_show.quote: The rib cage is broad, giving it a barrel chest, especially in comparison to less derived theropods like Ceratosaurus.

must_show.claim: Allosaurus had a long, slightly sloping tail.
must_show.quote: Allosaurus was a typical large theropod, having a massive skull on a short neck, a long, slightly sloping tail, and reduced forelimbs.

Allosaurus.why: Horns above eyes, barrel chest, long sloping tail; no sail or massive skull.

must_show.claim: Spinosaurus had a long, low, narrow skull like a crocodile's.
must_show.quote: The skull of Spinosaurus was long, low, and narrow, similar to that of a modern crocodilian, and bore straight conical teeth with few to no serrations.

must_show.claim: It had a sail on its back made of very long spines growing from its back bones.
must_show.quote: Very tall neural spines growing on the back vertebrae of Spinosaurus formed the basis of what is usually called the animal's "sail".

must_show.claim: Its long, narrow tail was deep and shaped like a paddle or fin.
must_show.quote: Coupled with the also elongated chevron bones on the underside of the caudals, this resulted in a deep and narrow tail with a paddle or fin-like shape, comparable to the tails of newts and crocodilians.

must_show.claim: It had a crest on its head shaped like a scimitar.
must_show.quote: Spinosaurus mirabilis had a weird crest on its head that looked like a scimitar.

Spinosaurus.why: Crocodile-like skull, back sail, paddle-like tail, head crest; no feathers or armour.

must_show.claim: Brachiosaurus had a disproportionately long neck.
must_show.quote: It had a disproportionately long neck, small skull, and large overall size, all of which are typical for sauropods.

must_show.claim: Brachiosaurus had longer forelimbs than hindlimbs.
must_show.quote: Atypically, Brachiosaurus had longer forelimbs than hindlimbs, which resulted in a steeply inclined trunk and a proportionally shorter tail.

must_show.claim: Its trunk was steeply inclined and its tail was proportionally shorter.
must_show.quote: Atypically, Brachiosaurus had longer forelimbs than hindlimbs, which resulted in a steeply inclined trunk and a proportionally shorter tail.

Brachiosaurus.why: Long neck, longer forelimbs, steep trunk and short tail.

must_show.claim: It had a long tail that ended like a whip.
must_show.quote: As in other diplodocids, the last portion of the tail of Brontosaurus possessed a whip-like structure.

must_show.claim: Its snout was squared off and low.
must_show.quote: Their snouts were squared off and low, in contrast to those of macronarians.

must_show.claim: Its back had an arched shape because the spines of its back bones grew taller toward the tail.
must_show.quote: The neural spines of the dorsals would increase in height further towards the tail, creating an arched back.

Brontosaurus.why: Whip-like tail, squared-off snout, arched back.

must_show.claim: Diplodocus was a very large, long-necked, four-legged animal with a long, whip-like tail.
must_show.quote: Among the best-known sauropods, Diplodocus were very large, long-necked, quadrupedal animals, with long, whip-like tails.

must_show.claim: Its head was short.
must_show.quote: It had a short 6 ft long head.

must_show.claim: Its tail was about 55% of its total body length.
must_show.quote: The estimated tail length of Diplodocus makes up approximately 55% of the total body length, with the tail sometimes hypothesized to be capable of functioning like a very long, tapering bullwhip.

Diplodocus.why: Whip-like tail, short head, tail about 55% of body length.

must_show.claim: Argentinosaurus was an enormous, long-necked, long-tailed, four-legged plant-eater.
must_show.quote: It was an enormous, long-necked, long-tailed, quadrupedal, plant-eater from Argentina, South America during the Cretaceous period.

must_show.claim: It moved on four legs.
must_show.quote:
How it moved:
on four legs

must_show.claim: It had a long tail.
must_show.quote: It was an enormous, long-necked, long-tailed, quadrupedal, plant-eater from Argentina, South America during the Cretaceous period.

Argentinosaurus.why: Long neck, long tail, four-legged stance.

must_show.claim: Amargasaurus had two parallel rows of tall spines down its neck and back.
must_show.quote: Most distinctively, it sported two parallel rows of tall spines down its neck and back, taller than in any other known sauropod.

must_show.claim: The spines on the neck were bowed backward and stuck up above the vertebra behind them.
must_show.quote: On the neck, they were bowed backward, projecting above the adjacent vertebra.

must_show.claim: The spines on the last two back vertebrae, the hip, and the front of the tail flared into a paddle shape at the top.
must_show.quote: The last two dorsal vertebrae, the hip, and the foremost tail in Amargasaurus also had elongated spines; these were not bifurcated but flared into a paddle-shaped upper end.

Amargasaurus.why: Two parallel rows of tall spines, neck spines bowed backward, paddle-shaped spines.

must_show.claim: Triceratops had a large bony frill.
must_show.quote: Bearing a large bony frill, three horns on the skull, and a large, four-legged body, exhibiting convergent evolution with rhinoceroses, Triceratops is one of the most recognizable of all dinosaurs and the best-known ceratopsian.

must_show.claim: Triceratops had three horns on its skull.
must_show.quote: Bearing a large bony frill, three horns on the skull, and a large, four-legged body, exhibiting convergent evolution with rhinoceroses, Triceratops is one of the most recognizable of all dinosaurs and the best-known ceratopsian.

must_show.claim: The front of the head had a large beak in front of its teeth.
must_show.quote: The front of the head was equipped with a large beak in front of its teeth.

Triceratops.why: Large bony frill, three horns, beak.

must_show.claim: Ankylosaurus had a wide, low skull.
must_show.quote: It had a wide, low skull, with two horns pointing backward from the back of the head, and two horns below these that pointed backward and down.

must_show.claim: Ankylosaurus had a large club on the end of its tail.
must_show.quote: It was covered in armor plates, or osteoderms, with bony half-rings covering the neck, and had a large club on the end of its tail.

must_show.claim: Ankylosaurus had a broad muzzle.
must_show.quote: Its broad muzzle indicates it was a non-selective browser.

must_show.claim: Ankylosaurus was covered in armor plates, with bony half-rings on its neck.
must_show.quote: It was covered in armor plates, or osteoderms, with bony half-rings covering the neck, and had a large club on the end of its tail.

covering: Ankylosaurus was covered in armor plates, with bony half-rings on its neck.
Ankylosaurus.why: Wide low skull, tail club, broad muzzle; armor plates.

must_show.claim: Stegosaurus had a double row of kite-shaped plates standing upright along its back.
must_show.quote: The quadrupedal Stegosaurus is one of the most easily identifiable dinosaur genera, due to the distinctive double row of kite-shaped plates rising vertically along the rounded back and the two pairs of long spikes extending horizontally near the end of the tail.

must_show.claim: Stegosaurus had two pairs of long spikes near the end of its tail.
must_show.quote: The quadrupedal Stegosaurus is one of the most easily identifiable dinosaur genera, due to the distinctive double row of kite-shaped plates rising vertically along the rounded back and the two pairs of long spikes extending horizontally near the end of the tail.

must_show.claim: Stegosaurus had a short neck and a small head.
must_show.quote: It had a short neck and a small head, meaning it most likely ate low-lying bushes and shrubs.

Stegosaurus.why: Double row of kite-shaped plates, tail spikes, short neck and small head.

must_show.claim: It stood and walked on two legs.
must_show.quote: Pachycephalosaurus was a bipedal herbivore, possessing long, strong legs and somewhat small arms with five-fingered hands.

must_show.claim: It had a large bony dome on top of its head.
must_show.quote: Pachycephalosaurus is famous for having a large, bony dome on top of its skull, up to 25 cm (10 in) thick, which safely cushioned its brain.

must_show.claim: Its head had a small muzzle that ended in a pointed beak.
must_show.quote: Pachycephalosaurus had a small muzzle that ended in a pointed beak.

Pachycephalosaurus.why: Bipedal stance, bony dome, small muzzle with pointed beak.

must_show.claim: Parasaurolophus had a long, distinctive head crest.
must_show.quote: Parasaurolophus was a duck-billed dinosaur with a long, distinctive head crest.

must_show.claim: The crest was a long curved tube that went upwards and back from the skull.
must_show.quote: They had a large head crest, which was a long curved tube. It went upwards and back from the skull.

must_show.claim: It had a beak and toothed jaws.
must_show.quote:
Teeth:
beak and toothed jaws

Parasaurolophus.why: Long tubular crest, beak and toothed jaws.

must_show.claim: Its tail was long and ended in a downward bend with a paddle-like fluke.
must_show.quote: Its tail was long and ended in a downward bend and a paddle-like fluke.

must_show.claim: Its skull was conical and tapered to a short snout that reached a little past the frontmost teeth.
must_show.quote: The skull of Mosasaurus is conical and tapers off to a short snout which extends a little beyond the frontmost teeth.

must_show.claim: Its rib cage was unusually deep and formed an almost perfect semicircle, giving a barrel-shaped chest.
must_show.quote: Compared to other mosasaurs, the rib cage of Mosasaurus is unusually deep and forms an almost perfect semicircle, giving it a barrel-shaped chest.

Mosasaurus.why: long tail with fluke, conical skull, deep barrel chest

must_show.claim: Kronosaurus had a short tail.
must_show.quote: Like all plesiosaurs, Kronosaurus has four paddle-like limbs, a short tail and, like most pliosaurids, a long head and a short neck.

must_show.claim: Kronosaurus had a long head.
must_show.quote: Like all plesiosaurs, Kronosaurus has four paddle-like limbs, a short tail and, like most pliosaurids, a long head and a short neck.

must_show.claim: The lower jaw bones joined in a long, spoon-shaped front part.
must_show.quote: The mandibular symphysis of Kronosaurus is elongated and spatulate (spoon-shaped), and like its close relatives Brachauchenius and Megacephalosaurus, it contains up to six pairs of teeth.

Kronosaurus.why: short tail, long head, spoon-shaped lower jaw

must_show.claim: It had a dorsal fin for stability in the water.
must_show.quote: It possessed a long tail with a low fin, suggesting it wasn't as fast as Jurassic Ichthyosaurs, but also possessed a dorsal fin for stability in the water.

must_show.claim: Its front limbs were longer than its back limbs.
must_show.quote: Noteworthy, however, is that each toe had more individual bones than is usual in reptiles, and the front limbs were longer than the back limbs, both adaptations typical of later ichthyosaurs.

must_show.claim: It had a sagittal crest on its skull.
must_show.quote: M. cornalianus has a sagittal crest associated with the expansion of the upper temporal fenestra.

Mixosaurus.why: dorsal fin, longer front limbs, sagittal crest

must_show.claim: Tylosaurus had an elongated tail that ended in a downturn supporting a two-lobed fin.
must_show.quote: As such, it had a streamlined body, an elongated tail ending with a downturn supporting a two-lobed fin, and two pairs of flippers.

must_show.claim: Tylosaurus had a long, toothless snout knob sticking out from its snout.
must_show.quote: The most recognizable characteristic of Tylosaurus is the elongated edentulous rostrum that protrudes from its snout, for which the genus is named.

must_show.claim: The head of Tylosaurus was strongly conical and its snout was longer than most mosasaurs.
must_show.quote: The head was strongly conical and the snout proportionally longer than most mosasaurs, with the exception of Ectenosaurus.

Tylosaurus.why: two-lobed tail fin, toothless snout knob, long conical snout

must_show.claim: Plesiosaurus had a long and slender neck.
must_show.quote: Measuring around 3.5 m (11 ft) long, it is distinguishable by its small head, long and slender neck, broad turtle-like body, a short tail, and two pairs of large, elongated paddles.

must_show.claim: Plesiosaurus had a broad turtle-like body.
must_show.quote: Measuring around 3.5 m (11 ft) long, it is distinguishable by its small head, long and slender neck, broad turtle-like body, a short tail, and two pairs of large, elongated paddles.

must_show.claim: Plesiosaurus had a U-shaped jaw.
must_show.quote: Its U-shaped jaw and sharp teeth would have been like a fish trap.

Plesiosaurus.why: long slender neck, broad turtle-like body, U-shaped jaw

must_show.claim: Elasmosaurus had an extremely long neck.
must_show.quote: Measuring 10.3 meters (34 ft) in length, Elasmosaurus would have had a streamlined body with paddle-like limbs, a short tail, a small head, and an extremely long neck.

must_show.claim: The skull would have been slender and triangular.
must_show.quote: The skull would have been slender and triangular, with large, fang-like teeth at the front, and smaller teeth towards the back.

must_show.claim: The paddles at the front were longer than those at the back.
must_show.quote: The paddles at the front (the pectoral paddles) were longer than those at the back (the pelvic paddles).

Elasmosaurus.why: extremely long neck, slender triangular skull, longer front paddles

must_show.claim: The skulls of adult Pterodactylus were long and thin.
must_show.quote: The skulls of adult Pterodactylus were long and thin, with about 90 narrow and conical teeth.

must_show.claim: The skull and jaws were straight.
must_show.quote: Another autapomorphy that Pterodactylus has is that the skull and jaws were straight, which are unlike the upwardly curved jaws seen in the related ctenochasmatids.

must_show.claim: The teeth went back from the tips of both jaws and got smaller farther from the jaw tips.
must_show.quote: The teeth extended back from the tips of both jaws, and became smaller farther away from the jaw tips.

Pterodactylus.why: Long thin straight skull with many small teeth; no crest shown.

must_show.claim: Pteranodon had no teeth in its long mouth.
must_show.quote: It had no teeth in its long mouth, and it had a small pouch like a pelican at the back of its jaw.

must_show.claim: The upper jaw, which was longer than the lower jaw, was curved upward.
must_show.quote: The upper jaw, which was longer than the lower jaw, was curved upward; while this normally has been attributed only to the upward-curving beak, one specimen (UALVP 24238) has a curvature corresponding with the beak widening towards the tip.

must_show.claim: Pteranodon had a big crest at the back of its head.
must_show.quote: Pteranodon had a big crest at the back of its head.

Pteranodon.why: Toothless long beak with upward-curved upper jaw and big head crest.

must_show.claim: Quetzalcoatlus had a long neck.
must_show.quote: Quetzalcoatlus had an unusually long neck, and when it stood on the ground it was as tall as a giraffe.

must_show.claim: It had a long beak with no teeth.
must_show.quote: The feeding habits of Quetzalcoatlus (which had a long beak with no teeth) are unknown.

must_show.claim: It had a crest at the base of the beak.
must_show.quote: At the base of the beak, formed from the premaxilla, was a crest, referred to by some authors as a sagittal crest.

must_show.claim: It was covered in hair-like filaments called pycnofibres.
must_show.quote: As a pterosaur, Quetzalcoatlus would have been covered in hair-like filaments called pycnofibres, and had extensive wing-membranes, which would have been distended by a long wing-finger.

covering: It was covered in hair-like filaments called pycnofibres.
Quetzalcoatlus.why: Long neck, long toothless beak, crest at beak base; pycnofibres.

must_show.claim: Rhamphorhynchus had a long tail.
must_show.quote: Rhamphorhynchus had a long tail, stiffened with ligaments, which ended in a small diamond-shaped rudder that helped provide stability while flying.

must_show.claim: The tail was stiffened with ligaments and ended in a soft-tissue tail vane.
must_show.quote: it had a long tail, stiffened with ligaments, which ended in a characteristic soft-tissue tail vane.

must_show.claim: The jaws had needle-like teeth angled forward and a curved, sharp, beak-like tip without teeth.
must_show.quote: The jaws of Rhamphorhynchus housed needle-like teeth, which were angled forward, with a curved, sharp, beak-like tip lacking teeth.

must_show.claim: Its body was covered with hairs.
must_show.quote: Like other pterosaurs, its body was covered with hairs, which suggests it had temperature regulation ('hot-blooded') and a high rate of metabolism.

covering: Its body was covered with hairs.
Rhamphorhynchus.why: Long stiff tail with vane and beak-tipped jaws with needle teeth.

must_show.claim: Dimorphodon had a large, bulky skull about 23 centimetres long.
must_show.quote: Dimorphodon had a large, bulky skull approximately 23 centimetres (9.1 in) in length, whose weight was reduced by large openings separated from each other by thin bony partitions.

must_show.claim: Dimorphodon had a big head, a small brain, a tall beak, and two types of teeth.
must_show.quote: It had a big head, a small brain, a tall beak, and two types of teeth.

must_show.claim: Dimorphodon had proportionally short wings.
must_show.quote: The body structure of Dimorphodon displays many "primitive" characteristics, such as, according to Owen, a very small brain-pan and proportionally short wings.

Dimorphodon.why: Large bulky tall-beaked skull, short wings, long tail.

must_show.claim: Titanoboa was a giant boid snake.
must_show.quote: Titanoboa (; lit. 'titanic boa') is a genus of extinct giant boid snake (being the biological family of all boas and anacondas) that lived during the middle and late Paleocene epoch.

must_show.claim: It was very long, with an estimated body length between 10.9 and 15.2 metres.
must_show.quote: It has an estimated body length between 10.9–15.2 m (36–50 ft), making it the largest known madtsoiid.
